The Fed and politicians in Congress caused the affordability crisis. Now politicians want to compound the error by fixing prices, increasing subsidies, and instituting new mandates. This isn’t a sustainable route to lowering living costs. It’s a recipe for more chaos.

Video

The rich pay the highest tax rates in the United States. The top 10% of income earners pay more than 60% of all federal taxes and 72% of income taxes, Cato’s @adamnmichel and @SantiagoForster explain.

ow.ly/eee850YHimG

Stung by groceries, electricity, and used car prices being almost 30% or more higher than in 2020, Americans now equate high prices with a poor economy. Politicians want to impose sector-by-sector interventions to provide relief. But most affordability proposals flunk basic economics, explains Cato’s @MrRBourne. 

On April 16, we are releasing the Cato “Handbook on Affordability,” featuring 100+ policy ideas to defuse inflation and lower the cost of living.

The 25th Amendment isn’t a tool for dealing with a controversial president—it’s a last resort for when a president cannot carry out the duties of the office. Urging the vice president to invoke it distracts from Congress’s existing power to check the president, says Cato’s Molly Nixon.

ow.ly/AJJF50YIo2R

US aluminum tariffs were supposed to boost security. Instead, they raised prices, hurt manufacturers, and pushed reliable Canadian producers away. With US smelters still closing and the Iran war denting supplies, the US is more vulnerable—not less. A policy own goal, explains Cato’s @scottlincicome.

ow.ly/G1Jx50YIbOs

Hungary tried national conservatism. The result: a lagging economy, rampant corruption, and a declining birth rate. Voters just delivered the verdict. Cato’s @johanknorberg explains what it means—and why it matters far beyond Hungary.

Video

Supporters said the Inflation Reduction Act would make Medicare drugs more affordable. Instead, CBO just raised its 10-year Medicare Part D spending projection by $600 billion. Cato scholar @mfcannon explains why government cost controls keep backfiring.

ow.ly/t2Ka50YHhV4

America’s electric power grid can’t keep up with demand. A new idea—Consumer-Regulated Electricity—would allow private, permissionless grids to expand energy faster and more efficiently, says Cato’s @ts_fisher.

Video

What can life on the front lines of criminal justice teach us about American law today? Join @RandyEBarnett for a discussion of his new memoir, Felony Review: Tales of True Crime and Corruption in Chicago, a gripping account of his years as a young prosecutor in the Cook County State’s Attorney’s Office in the late 1970s and early ’80s.

Register: ow.ly/iS2Y50YHctQ

More than half of federal revenue comes from income taxes, but the vast majority of Americans pay more payroll tax than income tax. 
  
Cato’s @adamnmichel and @SantiagoForster explain taxes in five charts: 
ow.ly/yrI950YHihX

Congress has just days to reauthorize FISA Section 702 — while the very oversight meant to prevent warrantless surveillance abuse has been systematically gutted. Cato Senior Fellow Patrick Eddington explains why a "clean" reauthorization is anything but.

ow.ly/iX9C50YHi6f

President Trump’s executive order challenges 150 years of birthright citizenship law, hinging on four words in the 14th Amendment. In the new Cato Podcast episode, @Thomas_A_Berry, Dan Greenberg, and @David_J_Bier unpack the constitutional stakes and what the justices signaled at oral arguments.

Apple: ow.ly/uwMZ50YH8am
Spotify: ow.ly/S91A50YH8ap
Our website: ow.ly/grsj50YH8aq

Advances in AI are driving an economic transition—the future will be marked by new jobs that demand new mixes of skills. One policy path forward is to improve labor matching. Too many skilled workers are missing out on better jobs because of poor signals and market flaws, explains Cato’s @KevinTFrazier.
ow.ly/3FnN50YH9B3

Since 2010, 500+ hospitals have closed obstetric units—so who delivers babies, especially in rural areas? 

States often restrict midwives and birthing centers with supervision rules and red tape, even as maternity deserts expand. 

Removing these barriers could improve access to prenatal care and safer deliveries, says Cato’s @dr4liberty. 
ow.ly/zpXz50YGIbc

One graph tells the story: satellite internet use in Argentina surged the moment the government lifted its ban. One deregulation. Millions connected. That's what getting government out of the way looks like. 

ow.ly/TQLH50YHizM

The NYT reports that powerful synthetic drugs produced in small labs are becoming a major force in today's illegal drug market. The lesson is simple: prohibition doesn’t stop drugs—it makes them stronger, riskier, and more deadly, says Cato’s @dr4liberty. 
ow.ly/b2B450YHapT

The new Section 122 tariffs are just as illegal as the previous ones, and for many of the same reasons, explains Cato’s @Thomas_A_Berry.
cato.org/blog/new-tariffs-ar…

We’ve warned since 1991 that there’s a disconnect between what students learn in school and what skills they’ll need to thrive as citizens and workers. Those warnings have resulted in buzzwords and reports but little substantive reform. 

The AI economic transition already underway demands a broader and sustained response per Cato’s @KevinTFrazier.
cato.org/commentary/weve-bee…

Autism diagnoses are rising—but much of it may be overdiagnosis. A broken Medicaid system rewards more labels and more therapy, driving billions in waste, fraud, and care that doesn’t always help the kids who need it most, report Cato’s @AdamOmaryPhD and @dr4liberty.
ow.ly/oFbY50YEvGn

Ludwig von Mises, one of the 20th century’s foremost champions of free markets, saw clearly that socialism isn’t merely inefficient—it’s inherently destructive. Decades of failed central planning have made his case undeniable.
